title: Basic syntax, conventions and the first program

videos.script: Lesson 1 ran a five-line program without reading it. This lesson reads it, and the rules behind each line. {{hello}} Every statement ends with a semicolon, and every piece of code sits inside a class. Leave out one semicolon and the compiler says so, one line later than you might expect. {{names}} Then names. The compiler accepts almost anything, and Java programmers agree on almost everything. A capital letter tells you a class, a lower-case one a method or a variable. One naming rule is enforced: a public class lives in a file with its name. {{comments}} Then comments, and the kind that a tool turns into web pages. {{jshell}} After that, jshell, for trying one line at a time. {{compact}} And last, the shortest program Java 25 allows, with no class written at all, and why this course still writes the long form. By the end you can read any small Java file and say what each line is for.
